land.text: French Guiana, made a French department by the Law on Departmentalization of 1946

successors.note: The page gives the year only. Whether Cliopatria's French Fourth Republic (1945..1957) or Fifth Republic shape contains French Guiana was not checked; a reviewer should.

capitals.name: Cayenne
capitals.note: Cayenne, founded by colonists in 1643, is the prefecture and the largest city (infobox); the page names no other seat. Occupied by the Portuguese 1809-1817.

correction.text: the coast between the Oyapock and the Maroni around Cayenne, drawn as Cliopatria's 1791 shape because the page gives no earlier extent: 'colonists founded Cayenne in 1643'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria draws the colony only in 1791, but the page dates the durable French presence to 1643 and the colony's extent in 1809 as 'from the Brazilian border to the Maroni' (conquest page). The 1791 coastal shape is used as the best-known extent; unverified for 1643-1790 (page budget). The 1503 'first French establishment' and the failed 1763 colonisation are on the page but not territorial.

19,565 km2, bbox 54.3 W to 51.7 W and 4.0 N to 5.8 N: the coastal strip between the Maroni and the Oyapock, the extent the 1809 conquest page gives ('from the Brazilian border to the Maroni River'). The French Guiana infobox gives 84,000 km2 (land 83,534) for the modern department, a ratio of 0.23: the shape is the settled coast, not the whole interior, and the page dates nothing in 1791. Cliopatria draws it for 1791 only, as a member of the Kingdom of France umbrella.

correction.text: the same coastal strip, continued: 1809-1817 occupied by Portugal (ledger), otherwise French; the interior is not drawn until Inini in 1930

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe continuing the shape through 1792-1929. The conquest page: the 1809 surrender covered the land 'from the Brazilian border to the Maroni River', returned to France in 1817 with the Oyapock as the frontier with Brazil. The late-19th-century Franco-Brazilian dispute (the short-lived Counani state, settled by Swiss arbitration 'largely in favour of Brazil') is undated on the page, so no border change is recorded.

correction.text: the whole of French Guiana: 'The territory of Inini was created, covering most of the interior' in 1930, beside the coastal colony

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: from 1930 the colony is the coast plus Inini, i.e. the modern department (84,000 km2 on the infobox). Ends with departmentalisation in 1946.

ledger.note: 1643: French colonists found Cayenne. The page says France 'did not establish a durable presence until colonists founded Cayenne in 1643'; it also records a 'first French establishment' in 1503 and the failed 1763 colonisation effort.

region.text: the coastal districts of Oyapok and Appruage (Saint-Georges-de-l'Oyapock is the gazetteer anchor)

ledger.note: 1808: the Anglo-Portuguese attack begins. 'On 15 December he attacked the coastal districts of' Oyapok and Appruage (Yeo's British squadron, which had joined the Portuguese force off Belem), taking them without resistance.

region.text: the coast from the Oyapock to the Maroni

ledger.note: 1809: Cayenne capitulates. Portuguese troops landed on 6 January, the main landing was at Pointe Mahury on 7 January, Hugues accepted capitulation on 11 January, and the force entered Cayenne on 14 January.

region.text: the surrendered territory 'from the Brazilian border to the Maroni River'

ledger.note: 1809: Portugal (with British ships) occupies French Guiana. The Portuguese 'continued to occupy it until returning the colony to France in 1817'; the Maroni was the border with British-held Surinam. No Portuguese annexation was made.

region.text: the colony restored to France, with the Oyapock as the Brazilian frontier

ledger.note: 1817: France repossesses Cayenne. 'On 8 November 1817, a French fleet arrived with Cayenne's new governor' (Claude Carra Saint-Cyr); the 1814 Treaty of Paris had decided the return, and the Final Act kept the Oyapock (Treaty of Utrecht, 1713) as the Portuguese border. A second page (French Guiana) says Portugal kept a military presence 'until 1817'.

region.text: 'The territory of Inini was created, covering most of the interior'

ledger.note: 1930: the interior is organised as the territory of Inini. The page dates its creation but not whether the interior was claimed or administered earlier; the shape before 1930 is the coastal strip only.

region.text: 'The Law on Departmentalization made French Guiana a French department again'

ledger.note: 1946: French Guiana becomes a department of France (the page gives the year only, and 'again', without naming the earlier departmental status).

wars.name: Portuguese conquest of French Guiana

zones.text: the coast from the Oyapock to the Maroni, surrendered at Cayenne

wars.outcome: Anglo-Portuguese victory: Cayenne taken between 6 and 14 January 1809 and occupied until the handover to France on 8 November 1817; the 1814 Treaty of Paris decided the return.
wars.note: Part of the Peninsular-War era Portuguese reprisal against France; the page gives the campaign as 15 December 1808 to 14 January 1809.

certainty.note: A coastal colony with no surveyed frontier; the page gives no extent.

The Oyapock frontier with Brazil is 'defined by the 1713 Treaty of Utrecht' (conquest page) and the Maroni with Surinam is a river, but the interior and the Franco-Brazilian dispute (Swiss arbitration, undated on the page) remain approximate.

sources.title: French Guiana
sources.note: Identity, Cayenne 1643, 1809, 1814, 1817, Inini 1930, departmentalisation 1946, infobox area 84,000 km2.

sources.title: Portuguese conquest of French Guiana
sources.note: The 1808-1809 campaign, Hugues' capitulation, the occupation to the handover of 8 November 1817, the Maroni-Oyapock extent.

notes: Cliopatria has this colony for the single year 1791 (Seshat fr_bourbon_k_2, member of the '(Kingdom of France)' umbrella). The dossier extends it to the colony's whole life 1643-1946 so that French Guiana is drawn in the years the French shapes do not cover it; the 1643-1790 and 1792-1929 keyframes reuse the 1791 coastal shape because the pages give no extents (unverified: page budget). Overlap to check: the Cliopatria shapes of the Kingdom of France, French Third and Fourth Republics may or may not contain Guiana; the gap-filler should compare. Undated on the pages: the Franco-Brazilian Counani/Contestado dispute and its Swiss arbitration, the Kourou 1763 expedition, deportations. Dutch and English occupations of Cayenne are not on the page. No dossier exists for the Counani state (late 19th century, short-lived).
